source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: After crossing the Kailasa mountain, that greatly powerful ten-necked demon Ravana reached the world of Indra.
verses.2: The sound of that demon army approaching from all sides reached the world of the gods, resembling the roar of a churning ocean.
verses.3: Having heard that Ravana had arrived, Indra moved from his seat and spoke to all the assembled gods there.
verses.4: He commanded the Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Vishvas, Sadhyas, and Maruts to prepare for battle against the evil-minded Ravana.
verses.5: Thus addressed by Indra, the gods, who were as mighty as Indra in battle and possessed great courage, armored themselves, filled with eagerness for the fight.
verses.6: Distressed and greatly frightened by Ravana, Indra indeed approached Vishnu and spoke these words.
verses.7: O Vishnu, how shall I act, for this demon of great valor and might, this powerful Rakshasa, is indeed approaching for battle.
verses.8: He is powerful due to the boon granted, and not for any other reason; therefore, that true word spoken by Brahma must indeed be fulfilled.
verses.9: Therefore, just as Namuchi, Vritra, Bali, Naraka, and Shambara were destroyed by me with the support of your strength, so too act now.
verses.10: Indeed, O Lord of gods, O Madhusudana, there is no other refuge or ultimate resort in the three worlds, with all their moving and non-moving beings, except for you.
verses.11: Indra acknowledges Rama as the glorious, eternal Narayana, the lotus-navelled one, by whom all these worlds, including Indra himself as the lord of gods, were established.
verses.12: Indra further states that all these three worlds, with their moving and non-moving beings, were created by the Lord, and at the end of an age, all beings ultimately merge back into Him.
verses.13: Indra implores the Lord of gods to reveal truly how He, even with the aid of His discus, intends to fight Ravana.
verses.14: Thus addressed by Indra, the Lord Narayana replied that there was no need for such great fear, and asked Indra to listen to His words.
verses.15: The Lord explained that this evil-souled Ravana is currently unconquerable by gods or asuras, and cannot be killed even if approached, due to the boon he has received.
verses.16: It is inherently observed that this exceedingly powerful demon, along with his sons, will certainly perform a great deed.
verses.17: O lord of gods, regarding what you told me to fight, I will not fight against that demon Ravana in battle.
verses.18: Vishnu does not return from battle without killing the enemy, and indeed, it is difficult to fulfill this desire now because Ravana is protected by boons.
verses.19: And O king of gods, O Shatakratu, I promise in your presence that I shall indeed be the cause of this demon's death.
verses.20: I alone will be the killer of Ravana along with his followers, and I will gladden the gods, knowing that the time has come; this truth has been told to you, O king of gods, husband of Shachi.
verses.21: O mighty one, fight fearlessly together with all.
verses.22: Knowing that the time had come, I depart; then, the Rudras along with the Adityas, Vasus, Maruts, and the two Ashvins, arrayed for battle, quickly sallied forth from the city towards the Rakshasas.
verses.23: In the meantime, at the end of the night, a roar was heard from all sides from Ravana's army, which was engaged in battle.
verses.24: Those mighty heroes, engaged in battle, looked at each other and advanced joyfully, intent only on the fight.
verses.25: Then, seeing that immense and inexhaustible great army at the forefront of the battle, agitation arose among the armies of the gods.
verses.26: Then, a terrible battle ensued among the gods, demons, and rakshasas, marked by tumultuous roars and the brandishing of various weapons.
verses.27: In the meantime, Ravana's valiant ministers, the rakshasas of terrible appearance, assembled for battle.
verses.28: Maricha, Prahasta, Mahaparshva, Mahodara, Akampana, Nikumbha, Shuka, and Sarana were among them.
verses.29: Also present were Samhlada, Dhumaketu, Mahadamshtra, Ghatodara, Jambumali, Mahahrada, and the rakshasa Virupaksha.
verses.30: Among the other rakshasas were Suptaghna, Yajnakopa, Durmukha, Dushana, Khara, Trishira, Karaviraksha, and Suryashatru.
verses.31: Surrounded by all these, namely Mahakaya, Atikaya, Devantaka, and Narantaka, was one of immense valor and strength.
verses.32: Indeed, Sumali, Ravana's grandfather, entered the army and, greatly enraged, destroyed all the hosts of gods with sharp, various weapons, just as the wind scatters clouds.
verses.33: O Rama, that army of gods, being killed by the night-wanderers, was driven away from all directions, just like deer are scattered by lions.
verses.34: In this interval, the brave eighth Vasu, renowned as Savitra, entered the battlefield.
verses.35: Likewise, the two Adityas of great valor, Tvashta and Pushan, armored and fearless, then entered the battle with their army.
verses.36: Then a battle took place between the gods and the demons, who were enraged and renowned for never retreating from combat.
verses.37: Then all those demons, using dreadful and various weapons, struck down the gods arrayed in battle by hundreds of thousands.
verses.38: And the gods, in battle, with their pure weapons, led the dreadful demons of great strength and valor to the abode of Yama.
verses.39: O Rama, in the meantime, a demon named Sumali, enraged and wielding various weapons, attacked that army.
verses.40: Greatly enraged, he destroyed the entire army of gods with his sharp, various weapons, just as the wind scatters a cloud.
verses.41: All the gods, being struck by the very terrible great showers of arrows and spears and javelins, could not stand firm together.
verses.42: Then, as the gods were being put to flight by Sumali, Savitra, the eighth among the Vasus, enraged, stood firm.
verses.43: The greatly effulgent Savitra, surrounded by his own chariot divisions, checked the attacking demon with his valor in battle.
verses.44: Then, a great and hair-raising battle occurred between those two.
verses.45: Then, in a moment, the chariot of Sumali, who, along with Vasu, did not retreat in battles, was struck down and overthrown by the great arrows of the very great-souled Vasu.
verses.46: Vasu, having destroyed Sumali's chariot which was covered with hundreds of arrows in battle, then took up his mace with his hand for the purpose of killing him.
verses.47: Then, Savitri's son Vasu, having firmly grasped that mace with its blazing tip resembling the staff of Yama, struck it down upon Sumali's head.
verses.48: That mace, resembling a falling meteor, shone as it descended upon him, like a great thunderbolt released by Indra roaring down upon a mountain.
verses.49: Then, neither his bone, nor head, nor flesh was seen, as the mace had reduced the slain Sumali to ashes on the battlefield.
verses.50: Having seen Sumali killed in battle, all those Rakshasas fled together from all sides, crying out to each other, and being driven away by Vasu, they could not stand firm.
